articles.body: in Expo Router, your folder structure is your navigation. _layout.tsx files decide how screens are shown (stack, tabs, modal), route groups like (tabs) organize screens without changing URLs, [id].tsx handles dynamic routes, and every screen is deep-linkable automatically. The basics take ten minutes to learn. This guide covers the patterns you actually need once the app has auth, tabs, modals and links coming in from outside. Most file-based routing tutorials stop at "create app/index.tsx and app/about.tsx ". Real apps need more: a tab bar that disappears on detail screens, a login flow nobody can skip, modals that work with the back gesture and push notifications that open the right screen. All of that is solvable with folder structure, once you know the patterns.

articles.title: Your agent's session store is a database nobody designed. Audit the five gaps.
articles.excerpt: A developer deleted a session from a Google ADK Go agent. The framework returned no error. The session row was gone. The password the agent had read from a config file was still sitting in the events…
articles.body: A developer deleted a session from a Google ADK Go agent. The framework returned no error. The session row was gone. The password the agent had read from a config file was still sitting in the events table, in plain text, attached to nothing. That is not a hypothetical. It is the opening of a post by davideimola on dev.to (2026-11-11), with a public reproduction: no model, no API key, just the session service doing what its runner does after a tool call. You delete, it returns nil, the events survive. The interesting part is not the bug. It is what the bug is a symptom of. Your agent's session store is a database. Nobody designed it as one, and your compliance obligations have already classified it as one.

articles.body: 在手机抓包中， 证书绑定 是一种让抓包工具“失灵”的安全机制。它会导致你在手机上安装了 Burp Suite 或 Charles 的 CA 证书后，目标 App 依然提示网络错误、连接失败或无法加载数据。 它是什么 正常情况下，App 信任手机系统里所有受信任的 CA 机构证书。抓包工具能解密 HTTPS，正是利用了这一点：你把抓包工具的证书装进手机，系统信任了它，App 也就跟着信任了。 证书绑定打破了这一逻辑。App 在代码里“写死”了它只认服务器那一张特定的证书或公钥。即使抓包工具的证书被系统信任，只要不是 App 预设的那一张，连接就会被强制断开。 抓包时的典型表现 当你设置好代理并安装证书后，如果 App 出现以下情况，通常意味着存在证书绑定： 提示“网络连接失败”、“网络异常”或“证书无效”。 App 闪退或卡在加载界面。 系统日志中可能出现类似 Pin verification failed 或 Certificate chain validation failed 的错误。 常见的绕过思路（仅供授权测试） 在获得合法授权的前提下，安全测试人员会通过动态插桩或修改安装包来绕过这一机制： 使用 Frida/Objection ：这是最常用的方法。通过注入脚本，Hook 掉校验证书的系统函数（如 Android 的 TrustManager 或 iOS 的 SecTrustEvaluate ），让校验函数永远返回“通过”。Objection 工具甚至提供了一键绕过命令（如 android sslpinning disable ）。 修改安装包（重打包） ：针对 Android，可以反编译 App，修改 network_security_config.xml 或直接删除校验代码，然后重新签名安装。 针对 Flutter 等特殊框架 ：如果 App 是用 Flutte…

articles.body: AI Cold Calling in 2026: The Real Numbers Behind Voice Agents Taking Over the Phone Here's the most uncomfortable number in B2B sales right now: the average cold call success rate (dial-to-meeting) fell from about 4.82% in 2024 to roughly 2.3% in 2025 — almost half in twelve months, according to Cognism's WHAM-powered State of Cold Calling 2025 report. Meanwhile, the same period saw the number of enterprises running AI voice agents for outbound jump from ~11% to 28–34% of mid-market and enterprise teams, per Auto Interview AI's 2026 tracking. Put those two lines together and you get the actual story of 2026: human cold calling is getting harder at the exact moment AI voice agents got cheap enough to deploy at scale. Both things are true at once.

articles.title: Front-channel logout is a browser workflow, not a revocation guarantee
articles.excerpt: Front-channel logout is a browser workflow, not a revocation guarantee Single sign-on makes login convenient and logout harder. A user may have sessions at an OpenID Provider and several relying parti…
articles.body: Front-channel logout is a browser workflow, not a revocation guarantee Single sign-on makes login convenient and logout harder. A user may have sessions at an OpenID Provider and several relying parties, each with its own cookie, token cache, and local session state. OpenID Connect Front-Channel Logout defines a browser-mediated way for the provider to ask relying parties to clear their sessions. It is useful, but it cannot be the only control an application relies on when access must end immediately. The front-channel specification uses the user agent to deliver logout requests to relying parties. The provider renders logout requests in the browser context, and the relying party responds according to the session state it can observe.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 12 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Moon, Venus and Spica Meet Explanation: Not all those who wander are lost. A night sky example is that planets wander, and in fact the very word “planet” comes from “wandering star” in Greek. As planets shift relative to fixed stars , they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions . They don’t happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics .

articles.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
articles.excerpt: NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for Mars Sample Return (MSR), called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture.
articles.body: A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled Mars Sample Return (MSR) program, called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture, or PSRA in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. The PSRA initiative was noted on Nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).
articles.author: Leonard David

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.
